subject: Requesting exec signoff: elevated uptime & latency guardrail for Prospero pilot
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot ask — elevated uptime + latency guardrail for Prospero (commercials attached)

Hannah —

Quick summary: Prospero is asking for a non-standard availability commitment for their pilot: target 99.995% monthly uptime and a 95th-percentile per-request latency SLO of 150ms for generation endpoints in us-west. In exchange they will sign a 24-month committed consumption contract with an initial $1.2M ARR commit and are asking for a 30% list-price discount for the first year.

They also want service credit terms that are tighter than our standard: accelerated remediation windows and a smaller cap on credits (they proposed unlimited up to x% of monthly invoice, but we pushed to a cap). Legal will mirror our standard indemnities. Prospero flagged compliance (SOC2) and wants accelerated monitoring hooks and a dedicated on-call routing for the pilot.

I've attached the draft term sheet (prospero_term_sheet_v1.pdf) and a simple credit impact model (credit-model.xlsx). Can you review and, if it looks reasonable, route to exec for signoff? Jonas — would appreciate deal desk guidance on acceptable credit caps and whether we take on the 150ms latency guardrail as-is or negotiate a phased approach.

Key asks:
- Exec signoff on 99.995% uptime + 150ms latency SLO for pilot (non-standard)
- Approval for 30% discount first-year conditional on 24-month commit (or counter-offer)
- Approval for proposed service credit cap and remediation cadence

Thanks — I can join a quick call if needed.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Pilot ask — elevated uptime + latency guardrail for Prospero (commercials attached)

Thanks Marissa —

Quick read: the commercial asks are material but also strategic. Prospero is a marquee customer in the AI-first healthcare vertical and the multi-year commit is valuable. Jonas, please confirm the financial exposure if we accept 99.995% + 150ms SLO and 30% discount. If we proceed, we'll need a limited, signed carveout:

- Service credit cap: no more than 20% of monthly invoice (recommendation)
- Remediation window: 48 hours to provide operational mitigation plan, 10 business days to deliver root cause and remediation steps
- Pilot duration: 90 days with a performance review at day 45 to determine go/no-go for ramp
- Monitoring: export of latency histograms + automated alert hooks to Prospero's PagerDuty (read-only)

If the numbers look acceptable, I want to send a short note to Vivek for executive signoff outlining the tradeoffs and attach Jonas's model.

Hannah

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-05-03T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot ask — elevated uptime + latency guardrail for Prospero (commercials attached)

Hannah / Marissa —

I ran the credit-model and pulled in Ops numbers. Short summary and recommendation:

Impact (estimated, conservative):
- Worst-case monthly credit exposure if we accept 99.995% without additional guardrails: ~ $36k (about 3% of expected monthly invoice at their committed level).
- With a 20% cap on credits and the phased performance review (45/90 days), exposure drops to approx $9k/month.
- Meeting 150ms 95th will require a dedicated pool during their peak window (us-west), estimated incremental monthly infra delta ~$7k — we can absorb first 3 months as onboarding cost and then back-charge or amortize into price.

Recommended commercial structure (deal desk):
1) Approve elevated SLOs for pilot only (90-day pilot) — not a permanent contractual SLO until post-pilot review.
2) Discount: approve up to 25% first-year if they commit to 24 months (counter to 30%).
3) Service credit cap: 20% of monthly invoice; credits accrue monthly and are offset against future invoices only (no cash refunds).
4) Ops conditions: dedicated routing + deployment isolation for pilot; automated telemetry export; playbook with 48-hour mitigation window.
5) Legal: add a sunset clause making the elevated SLOs expire at the end of pilot unless both parties sign a formal amendment.

If this is acceptable, we should send a short exec summary to Vivek asking for signoff on the temporary, pilot-only SLO + 25% discount cap. I've attached the model (credit-model.xlsx).

-Jonas
Deal Desk Manager
jonas@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Pilot ask — elevated uptime & latency guardrail for Prospero pilot — Exec signoff

Team —

Thanks for the summary and the clear recommendations. I approve the proposed path with the following conditions:

1) Pilot-only exception: Approve the 99.995% uptime target and the 150ms 95th latency guardrail for a 90-day pilot only. This will not become an evergreen contractual SLO without a signed amendment post-pilot.
2) Discount cap: Approve up to 25% first-year discount tied to the 24-month commit (Jonas recommendation). Do not go to 30% on initial offer.
3) Service credit cap: Approve the 20% monthly invoice cap on credits, credits applied only as invoice offsets.
4) Infrastructure cost: Redwood will absorb up to the first 3 months of incremental infra costs for the dedicated pool; thereafter, costs are to be amortized into the agreed MRR or handled via a surcharge.
5) Escalation & reporting: Prospero must accept our incident post-mortem cadence and confidentiality arrangement. Ops must provide a weekly status digest during the pilot to both Prospero and our exec sponsor.

Please send Prospero a one-page confirmation and attach the term sheet with the changes circled. Hannah/Marissa — copy Legal on the outbound and loop in CS for onboarding.

Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Revenue, Redwood Inference
